para: The graph is not merely a representation of known results: it is a research tool that generates new ones. Its connectivity structure is itself informative. Two calculi that appear to have no relationship when studied in isolation may prove to be connected by a path of extension and embedding edges of modest length; such a path establishes a chain of translations that may or may not be composable into a direct translation between the two endpoints. When a direct translation exists, the path constitutes a proof of its existence; when no direct translation can be composed from the available edges, the obstruction is localized to a specific step in the path, and the analysis of that obstruction becomes a well-defined proof-theoretic problem rather than an open-ended search. The graph thus converts the vague question Are these two logics related? into the precise question What is the shortest path between these two nodes, and do the edge types along it compose?
